executive_summary: The fleet coordination bus (public.session_coordination, 5254 rows, carrying fleet-control primitives) grants TRUNCATE to authenticated, and TRUNCATE is the one write-class operation RLS cannot gate. Every premise below was measured live before being written. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE SD TEXT ARE ENCODED HERE: anon holds no TRUNCATE at all (the exposure is authenticated-only), and FR-3/FR-4 substantially duplicate a migration ALREADY STAGED under SD-LEO-INFRA-COORDINATION-BUS-ACCESS-001, so this SD narrows to FR-1+FR-2 and verifies-and-records the rest rather than authoring a rival file against the same object. Zero DDL applied by the builder; the revoke is staged for the chairman ceremony.

functional_requirements.title: Stage the revoke of TRUNCATE AND the latent write grants on authenticated — chairman-gated, never applied
functional_requirements.description: MEASURED via information_schema.role_table_grants on public.session_coordination: anon = REFERENCES, SELECT, TRIGGER; authenticated = DELETE, INSERT, REFERENCES, SELECT, TRIGGER, TRUNCATE, UPDATE; service_role and postgres = full (OUT OF SCOPE per the SD Deletion Audit — do not touch the workers' path). CORRECTION TO THE SD TEXT: FR-1 as written says REVOKE ... FROM anon, authenticated. anon holds NO TRUNCATE and no write grants of any kind, so that half is a no-op. Harmless to issue, but the SD reads as though anon is an exposure on this table and it is not; the deliverable targets authenticated. WHY TRUNCATE SPECIFICALLY, which sharpens the requirement: RLS is ON (rowsecurity=true, force=false) with exactly ONE policy — service_role_full_access, cmd=SELECT, PERMISSIVE, roles=PUBLIC, USING true. authenticated INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE are therefore already DENIED by RLS because no policy covers those commands. TRUNCATE is not an RLS-checked operation, so it is the single write-class path RLS cannot stop — which is exactly why the sourcing probe saw TRUNCATE succeed under an otherwise-blocking posture. THE LATENT GRANTS ARE IN SCOPE, AND THE REASONING IS THE COORDINATOR'S (reply 323019d9), not mine — an earlier draft of this PRD deliberately UNBUNDLED them as a follow-on and that was the weaker call. The DELETE/INSERT/UPDATE grants are dormant only while no policy covers those commands. Add an INSERT or UPDATE policy for authenticated later and every dormant grant goes live in the same instant. That is safety-by-coincidence with a trigger condition someone will plausibly meet WHILE TRYING TO FIX SOMETHING ELSE, and the safety depends on a policy nobody has been told is load-bearing. So the revoke covers them — not because they are exploitable today, but because nothing would notice when they become so. DELIVERABLE: database/chairman-gated/<date>_session_coordination_revoke_authenticated_writes.sql plus a _DOWN companion, revoking TRUNCATE, DELETE, INSERT and UPDATE from authenticated, staged and committed, NEVER applied by the builder — not even inside a rolled-back transaction. Read-only validation is the permitted substitute. The _DOWN must restore exactly the four grants named, so the revert is precise rather than a blanket re-grant.

functional_requirements.title: Two-sided acceptance in ONE suite: TRUNCATE refused AND the bus still works
functional_requirements.description: Both halves must be green in a single run, and the SECOND half is the load-bearing one. (a) NEGATIVE: a TRUNCATE attempt as authenticated is REFUSED — exercised either transaction-wrapped against the live table or against a scratch table mirroring the grant posture, so the 5254 live rows are never at risk. (b) POSITIVE: after the revoke, every RLS-permitted operation for each role STILL SUCCEEDS — a legitimate signal INSERT via service_role lands and is readable, and the anon SELECT path returns rows. WHY (b) IS NOT OPTIONAL: session_coordination is the live fleet coordination bus. A revoke that silences it converts a confidentiality/integrity exposure into an availability outage, which is strictly worse than the exposure it fixes. A suite that proves only the refusal would ship that outage wearing a green test — the exact shape of a check that cannot fail in the direction that matters.

functional_requirements.title: File-vs-live drift: VERIFY and RECORD against the already-staged migration, do not author a rival
functional_requirements.description: VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY, and the SD's citation is misfiled. There is no database/migrations/20260309_session_coordination.sql. The real file is supabase/ehg_engineer/migrations/20260309_session_coordination.sql:67-70, and it ships CREATE POLICY "service_role_full_access" ON session_coordination FOR ALL USING (true) WITH CHECK (true) — with NO TO clause. Live is polcmd='r' (SELECT only) with polwithcheck NULL. THE DRIFT IS REAL; only the path was wrong. CORRECTED PREMISE (coordinator reply 323019d9): I first reasoned that this belonged to COORDINATION-BUS-ACCESS-001 as a live owner to coordinate with. That SD is COMPLETED (status=completed, claim-free, 2026-08-03T12:54:16Z), so there is NO live owner. The dedupe test is therefore 'do not duplicate what BUS-ACCESS already SHIPPED' — checkable at main — not 'wait for another builder'. What it shipped is a STAGED file, database/chairman-gated/20260803_session_coordination_scope_anon_reads.sql, whose header records this exact drift as UNRECONCILED, MUST BE SETTLED AT THE PRE-APPLY CAPTURE. So the drift is NOT resolved by anyone, and it is mine to resolve or to name out-of-scope — deferring it to a completed SD would be deferring to nobody. DELIVERABLE: the verification is recorded (sd.metadata.mechanism_verifications, four entries including the corrected path). The drift RESOLUTION is scoped OUT of this SD and stated as such rather than implied: reauthoring or retiring that migration file changes what a future reader believes about a policy whose live shape is still disputed between two captures, and settling that dispute belongs with the pre-apply capture the existing staged file already demands. What this SD adds is that the dispute is now independently confirmed by a third reading and attributed, instead of resting on one prior capture. THE GENERALISING ROOT CAUSE, credited to that file's header and NOT to this SD: a CREATE POLICY with no TO clause defaults to PUBLIC. The name service_role_full_access states the author's intent accurately; the omitted TO service_role is the defect. Every CREATE POLICY in this repo lacking an explicit TO is silently public — a far larger finding than this table, and worth its own sweep.

functional_requirements.title: Anon-read posture: record the decision as already-routed, and check any SELECT narrowing for counting subqueries
functional_requirements.description: MEASURED: the single PUBLIC SELECT policy is the direct and sufficient cause of the anon-read finding — anon can SELECT every signal body on the bus. The SD requires this be surfaced as a NAMED DECISION and never folded silently. IT IS ALREADY ROUTED: the staged 20260803_session_coordination_scope_anon_reads.sql implements the narrowing under COORDINATION-BUS-ACCESS-001, awaiting the chairman ceremony. This SD therefore RECORDS the decision as routed-and-pending rather than re-deciding it or staging a second implementation. THE COUPLING CHECK THE SD EXPLICITLY DEMANDS, carried forward from SD-LEO-INFRA-THREE-GAPS-APPLIED-001: a counting subquery inside an RLS expression runs under the calling role's SELECT RLS, so narrowing SELECT anywhere can silently starve a count and flip a limit from binding to permitting. The anon-reads narrowing IS a SELECT narrowing, so it must be checked for counting subqueries before apply. The instrument is already on main: lib/policy/severity-pair-coupling.js and scripts/severity-pair-divergence-fence.mjs. Note this is a PRE-APPLY check owed by whoever runs the ceremony, not a code change here.

technical_requirements.title: Zero DDL applied by the builder
technical_requirements.description: Staged files only, plus read-only validation (BEGIN; SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY; ...; ROLLBACK). The chairman applies. This holds even inside a rolled-back transaction — staging is the deliverable, not an intermediate step.

technical_requirements.title: service_role is untouched
technical_requirements.description: Per the SD Deletion Audit, service_role grants are the workers' path and explicitly out of scope. The staged revoke names authenticated only, and the grant-posture readback reports service_role explicitly as unchanged rather than omitting it.

technical_requirements.title: The live table is never at risk during acceptance
technical_requirements.description: The TRUNCATE attempt is transaction-wrapped or run against a grant-posture-mirroring scratch table. 5254 live rows on a fleet-control bus are not an acceptable blast radius for a negative test.

test_scenarios.scenario: Grant posture readback shows no TRUNCATE for authenticated
test_scenarios.expected: After apply, information_schema.role_table_grants shows authenticated without TRUNCATE; anon unchanged at REFERENCES/SELECT/TRIGGER; service_role explicitly reported unchanged. Before apply, it still shows TRUNCATE — proving staged-not-applied.
The attempt raises insufficient_privilege. Transaction-wrapped or against a mirroring scratch table; the live table row count is unchanged before and after.

test_scenarios.scenario: The bus still works — service_role send/read path
test_scenarios.expected: A legitimate signal INSERT via service_role lands and is readable afterwards. THE LOAD-BEARING HALF: a failure here means the revoke broke coordination.

test_scenarios.scenario: The bus still works — anon SELECT path
test_scenarios.expected: anon SELECT still returns rows after the revoke (subject to whatever the separately-staged anon-reads narrowing later decides). Confirms the revoke did not disturb the read path.
TS-2 and TS-3/TS-4 execute in a single suite invocation. Splitting them across runs is how a green refusal ships alongside a dead bus.

test_scenarios.scenario: Staged migration is committed and NOT applied
test_scenarios.expected: The revoke file and its _DOWN companion exist in database/chairman-gated/ and are committed, while the live grant posture still shows TRUNCATE for authenticated. Evidence rows for this SD show ddl_applied=0.

test_scenarios.scenario: No rival migration was authored against session_coordination
test_scenarios.expected: database/chairman-gated/ contains exactly one NEW file from this SD (the revoke). The pre-existing 20260803_session_coordination_scope_anon_reads.sql is untouched and referenced, not duplicated or superseded.

acceptance_criteria: FR-2 both halves green in ONE run — TRUNCATE refused AND every RLS-permitted path still succeeding.

Grant posture readback shows no TRUNCATE (and no unjustified write grants) for anon/authenticated on session_coordination after the chairman apply; before it, the posture is unchanged, proving staged-not-applied.
The 20260309 file's misdescription of live state is RECORDED with its verification and pointed at the existing staged migration — not fixed by a second staged file against the same object.
The anon-read posture decision is recorded with evidence as ALREADY ROUTED under SD-LEO-INFRA-COORDINATION-BUS-ACCESS-001, explicitly not re-decided and not silently absorbed.
Zero DDL applied by the builder; service_role grants untouched; the live 5254-row table unharmed by any acceptance step.
The pre-apply coupling check is stated as owed: any SELECT narrowing must be checked for counting subqueries that would silently change meaning.

risks.risk: The revoke breaks the coordination bus, converting a confidentiality exposure into a fleet-wide availability outage.
risks.mitigation: FR-2's positive half is mandatory and in the same suite. A refusal-only test cannot detect this.

risks.risk: A second staged migration against session_coordination merges clean and then mutually reverts with the existing one.
risks.mitigation: FR-3/FR-4 verify-and-record only. TS-7 asserts exactly one new staged file from this SD.

risks.risk: The dormant DELETE/INSERT/UPDATE grants on authenticated become live the instant someone adds a policy covering those commands — plausibly while fixing something unrelated.
risks.mitigation: IN SCOPE, per coordinator 323019d9. An earlier draft unbundled these as a follow-on; that was weaker. Their safety currently depends on the ABSENCE of a policy, and nobody has been told that absence is load-bearing. The staged revoke names all four grants, and the _DOWN restores exactly those four.

risks.risk: Revoking four grants in one chairman apply has a wider blast radius than revoking one.
risks.mitigation: Accepted deliberately, and it is the reason FR-2's positive half covers every RLS-permitted path rather than only the one TRUNCATE touches. The _DOWN is grant-precise, so a revert restores the prior posture exactly rather than blanket re-granting.

risks.risk: The acceptance TRUNCATE damages the live 5254-row bus.
risks.mitigation: TR-3 — transaction-wrapped or scratch-table mirroring, with a row-count assertion before and after.

risks.risk: The builder applies the DDL to verify it works.
risks.mitigation: TR-1 plus read-only validation. TS-6 asserts the live posture is UNCHANGED at merge time, which is only true if nothing was applied.

integration_operationalization.consumers: The entire worker fleet reads and writes this bus via service_role (roll-call, signals, coordinator directives). anon holds SELECT only. The table carries fleet-control primitives including the enforcement kill-switch sentinel, so both confidentiality and availability matter.
integration_operationalization.dependencies: SD-LEO-INFRA-COORDINATION-BUS-ACCESS-001 owns the anon-read narrowing already staged against this same table; the chairman ceremony is the only path that applies either file; QF-20260803-856 is writing the ceremony checklist (path fence -> @approved-by matching git user.email -> git-committed -> MIGRATION_APPLY_TOKEN -> post-conditions).
integration_operationalization.data_contracts: No schema change. Grant-only: REVOKE TRUNCATE ON public.session_coordination FROM authenticated. No policy is created, altered or dropped by this SD.
integration_operationalization.runtime_config: No new env vars. MIGRATION_APPLY_TOKEN is consumed by the chairman ceremony, not by this SD.
integration_operationalization.observability_rollout: Two staged files (revoke + _DOWN) merge to git and wait. The grant-posture readback is runnable before and after apply and is the observable: before, authenticated shows TRUNCATE; after, it does not. That before/after difference is the proof the ceremony ran, and it is why the readback ships even though the revoke does not self-apply.

system_architecture.objects_touched: public.session_coordination grants only. Policy inventory read but not modified: a single PERMISSIVE SELECT policy named service_role_full_access bound to PUBLIC with USING true.
system_architecture.invariant: RLS cannot gate TRUNCATE. Any role holding TRUNCATE on an RLS-protected table has an ungatable destructive path regardless of how carefully the policies are written.
system_architecture.coupling_map: authenticated's dormant DELETE/INSERT/UPDATE grants <- absence of a policy covering those commands (breaks the moment one is added). The anon-reads narrowing <- any counting subquery running under anon's SELECT RLS (the fails-open class from THREE-GAPS-APPLIED-001).

implementation_approach.sequence: Write the grant-posture readback first so the before-state is captured and the after-state is checkable. Then the two-sided acceptance suite (negative and positive together). Then stage the revoke + _DOWN. Then record FR-3/FR-4 verifications pointing at the existing staged file.
implementation_approach.verification_discipline: Measure before encoding — four premises in the SD text moved under measurement during LEAD, two of them materially. Prove the positive half of acceptance, not only the refusal.
implementation_approach.out_of_scope: service_role grants; redesigning the bus or its archive flow; the signal-swallowing fix (SIGNAL-ROUTER-AUTO-001 owns it); implementing an anon-read narrowing (already staged elsewhere); revoking the dormant DELETE/INSERT/UPDATE grants (candidate follow-on, deliberately unbundled).

smoke_test_steps.expected_outcome: One line per role. Pre-apply: authenticated still shows TRUNCATE (proving staged-not-applied). Post-apply: authenticated shows no TRUNCATE, anon unchanged at REFERENCES/SELECT/TRIGGER, service_role explicitly reported unchanged. Non-zero exit if any write-class grant reappears for anon or authenticated.

smoke_test_steps.instruction: Run the two-sided acceptance suite: npx vitest run tests/integration/session-coordination-truncate-posture.db.test.js
smoke_test_steps.expected_outcome: BOTH halves green in one run: a TRUNCATE attempt as authenticated is REFUSED, AND a legitimate service_role send/read plus the anon SELECT path still succeed. A run where the refusal passes but the bus paths fail is the failure this step exists to catch.

smoke_test_steps.instruction: Confirm staged-not-applied: git status --porcelain database/chairman-gated/ then re-run step 1
smoke_test_steps.expected_outcome: The revoke file and its _DOWN companion are committed in database/chairman-gated/, and step 1 STILL reports authenticated holding TRUNCATE — proving the builder staged rather than applied. The posture changes only after the chairman ceremony.
